Shield rows reuse the same Realistic build with the weapon slot swapped to the top level 70 one-hander (7x attack lessers) and a Gold Ancient Shield added (7x Shield DEF lessers; its 29% guard chance is already inside the EHP number). Their S/A/B grades and column colors use the ten base-build ranges. Those ten builds also set table sorting and the DPS rankings guide. Mobility, Support, and Range repeat the base values because the character is the same.

Methodology and limits

Damage: ST DPS and AoE DPS use the saved level 70 Realistic builds, their exact skill allocations, and a 0-defense target. Neutral is the default. Favorable applies the current weak or undead result to supported elemental attacks. Physical and non-elemental attacks stay unchanged. This is not an average of elemental uptime. DPS assumes enough MP or HP for continuous casting, and short success-only buffs appear as separate ceilings.

Damage/MP: The selected target mode's ST damage per use is divided by its MP cost. Recovery, MP Eater, potions, ammunition, buff activation costs, and HP costs are excluded.

EHP: Physical and magic EHP use the same builds against level 70 Tauromacis, with full bars and allocated defensive buffs active. The result includes defenses, expected physical misses, eligible shield guards, and Magic Guard where allocated. Healing, recovery procs, potions, control, range, and attack costs are excluded. HP and MP follow the measured level-growth table, apply each class's listed advancement bonus at levels 10 and 30, then add saved gear. Percentage-skill intermediates are truncated, and EHP is rounded to the nearest 10. Magic Guard rows model HP plus MP as one shared survival pool. Empty-MP spillover behavior is not independently verified.

Capability ratings: Mobility, Support, and Range are separate 1-5 judgments based on the saved first-job and second-job allocations and attack geometry. All 109 positive allocations were classified as applied, checked as direct-attack candidates, or excluded. Excluded effects include Final Attack procs, persistent damage, healing and recovery, reflection, ammunition economy, and effects inactive with the saved weapon.

Grades and colors: The table recalculates values, sorting, grades, and colors for the selected target mode. Within each column, red is the lowest observed value, yellow is the midpoint, and green is the highest. The S/A/B label divides that same observed range into upper, middle, and lower thirds. Equal values receive the same grade. Color and grade are visual aids; the exact number remains the comparison.

No composite score or overall class grade is applied. Islander is a Beginner challenge outside the second-job comparison, so every column shows N/A.

Grummash created the 10 Realistic level 70 builds. We use MeowDB-owned copies with the same equipment and skill allocations. The class DPS rankings guide has all 10 build cards, every allocated direct-attack row, per-cast result, cast rate, and one-minute output.

How to Use This Comparison

Start with the job you want to play. Use the table to compare its tradeoffs, then open the class card before making the choice.

  1. Pick the part of play you care about. Solo grinding draws on AoE DPS, Mobility, Range, and survival. Boss damage starts with ST DPS and Damage/MP. Party value lives in Support and the skill notes.
  2. Sort those columns. A class can lead one result and trail another. The table never combines them into a hidden overall score.
  3. Open the finalists. Each class card explains the saved skills, target limits, active buffs, and exclusions behind its row.

Map layout, travel, potion use, and party composition sit outside this benchmark. Your weapon, AP, SP, shield, and scrolls can also move the result. Check the linked build or the Damage Simulator before judging the gear you plan to use.
